Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary: Young adult with several days of constant, worsening suprapubic pain (8/10) associated with light intermenstrual bleeding and slight discharge; sexually active with implant contraception; LMP ~2–3 weeks ago; last pregnancy test ~1 month ago. No fever, vomiting, shoulder-tip pain, syncope, or urinary dysuria. Constipation last week has resolved. No exam or labs performed.  
- Working diagnosis: Acute pelvic pain with intermenstrual bleeding—rule out pregnancy-related causes (including ectopic) and pelvic pathology.  
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx and transcript):
  - Ectopic pregnancy: Must be excluded urgently given pelvic pain and spotting; implant failure rare but possible; no pregnancy test since symptom onset.
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID): Pelvic pain with slight discharge and spotting in a sexually active patient; absence of fever does not exclude.
  - Functional/hemorrhagic ovarian cyst (including rupture): Acute pelvic pain and intermenstrual spotting; implant users can develop functional cysts.
  - Consider: Acute appendicitis (less typical localization; no fever), urinary tract infection/cystitis (less likely without dysuria/urgency).  
- Plan:
  - Arrange urgent face-to-face clinical assessment for abdominal and pelvic examination as discussed.
  - Perform pregnancy test today (urine). If positive, urgent same-day evaluation is required.
  - Safety-net: Seek urgent care if pain escalates, develops dizziness/syncope, shoulder-tip pain, fever, heavy bleeding, or inability to keep fluids down.
  - Further in-person workup to consider: pelvic exam (CMT/adnexal tenderness), urinalysis and urine culture if indicated, NAAT for STIs (chlamydia/gonorrhea) if PID suspected, serum/urine β-hCG, pelvic transvaginal ultrasound if β-hCG positive or if clinical concern for ectopic/cyst, CBC/CRP if infection suspected.  
- Conflict noted: None between transcript and listed DDx impressions.

- Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) — Likelihood: Medium. Lower abdominal pain with slight discharge/spotting in a sexually active patient; may occur without fever.
